item.semiconductor-lab.theodolite.note1: Measures how far away something is without going there. Sight the same mark from two places and the triangle tells you the distance.
item.semiconductor-lab.theodolite.note2: Telescope + vernier caliper (vernier scale) + 2 bronze + 2 sticks. Hold right-click to look, release to read the direction. 1) sight a mark and release (station A) -> 2) walk at least 3 m sideways, sight the same mark and release (station B) -> the base and two angles give the distance. Sneak + right-click clears station A.
item.semiconductor-lab.theodolite.note3: In 1615 the Dutchman Snellius measured the distance between towns with a chain of triangles (triangulation). Measure one base line carefully and angles alone do the rest of the country. In the 18th century the theodolite combined a telescope with graduated circles.
item.semiconductor-lab.theodolite.note4: Sine rule: with base c and end angles alpha and beta, distance from B = c sin(alpha) / sin(alpha + beta). The thinner the triangle (far target, short base), the more a small angle error grows. Ino Tadataka (1800-1821) mapped Japan by combining walked traverses with sightings of mountain peaks from many places.
item.semiconductor-lab.theodolite.placeh: Approximation: the base length is taken directly as the distance between the two stations (really it was measured on the ground with chains or rods). No link to map items yet.
item.semiconductor-lab.theodolite.statio: 📐 Station A recorded: bearing %s°. Walk sideways and sight the same mark
item.semiconductor-lab.theodolite.short_: The base is only %s m. Move at least %s m away first
item.semiconductor-lab.theodolite.no_cro: The two sight lines do not cross ahead. Did you sight the same mark? (station A kept)
item.semiconductor-lab.theodolite.result: 📐 Base %s m, angle A %s°, angle B %s° -> %s m from here to the target (at %s, %s)
item.semiconductor-lab.theodolite.real: The block you sighted is really %s m away (off by %s m)
